answer: Persistent Liability Ledger: each identity's actions mint a transferable jade obligation token that any counterparty can claim against the operator's shared collateral pool. Cloning forces the attacker to post fresh collateral per clone, since obligations from one clone can drain collateral backing all others—a quartz-tier deposit each. Honest agents reuse one identity, paying the cost once. A fable-like audit trail links obligations to pool drawdown, so N clones multiply deposit cost by N while honest cost stays fixed.
